what: vm-diag-snapshot.yml's failure comment confidently names the WRONG cause. On run 35649903349 it said 'The request parsed fine, so this is an infrastructure failure' and suggested VM_SSH_KEY / DIAG_READ_TOKEN unset or mismatched. MEASURED from the job log by the E19 lane: the SSH+curl round-trip to the VM SUCCEEDED (6 lines returned, no curl/ssh error), and the run died one step later in pure local Python -- ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scripts', because the issues-triggered path never ran actions/checkout. No secret was ever involved.
why_it_matters: An error message that names a wrong cause with confidence is worse than a generic one: it sends the reader to the one class of fix a session CANNOT perform (originating a secret value is operator-only), so the honest response to it is to stop and ask a human. It cost a real measurement -- the E16 lane could not read prop_status_request's cadence state and had to INFER which ask-arm fired -- and the batched path had been broken since 2026-09-13 (a45d360 added the scripts.* import with no checkout), nine days, with nobody diagnosing it because the message looked authoritative.
